title: Cold-email reply classification
about: Every outbound team triages replies: book the interested ones, snooze the not-nows, follow the referrals, and never email the opt-outs again. The costly mistake is treating a polite "please take me off your list" as a plain "no thanks". Removal is asked as its own question so no intent can override it.

rules: Skip contacts on the suppression list.
Send text that looks like an instruction to the model to a person.
Reply contains "unsubscribe", "remove me" or "opt out": suppress without asking Jev.
0_filter_and_cache.cache: Answer store. Fingerprint = questions + model + state; a stored answer is reused with no Jev call.

intent.instructions: What is the sender of `reply` telling us, in response to the cold email in `our_email`?

criteria.interested: Wants to talk, asks for a meeting, times or more information
criteria.not_now: Open to it but explicitly later, or asks to be contacted again at a future time
criteria.referral: Points us to a different person who handles this
criteria.objection: Engages but pushes back on price, fit, timing or an existing vendor
criteria.not_interested: Declines without asking to be removed
criteria.out_of_office: An automatic away or out-of-office message
criteria.unsubscribe: Asks to stop receiving emails or to be removed

wants_removal.instructions: Does `reply` ask, in any wording, to stop being contacted or to be removed from the list?

criteria.true: Any request to stop, remove, unsubscribe or not be contacted again

names_another_person.instructions: Does `reply` name or point to a different person we should contact instead?

rules: wants_removal at or above the cutoff suppresses, whatever the intent.
A customer asking for removal goes to the account owner instead of silently onto the list.
Referral: a regex copies the address from the reply; Jev only decides that a referral exists.
Otherwise act on intent: interested books, not_now snoozes, out_of_office retries, the rest close.
unsure: A referral with no address in the reply.
A customer asking to be removed.

actions.suppress: Write suppressed = true to the facts for that email. Every playbook reads it in step 0.
actions.extract_contact: Push the referred contact to the SDR queue.

4_act.ledger: Every record is logged with its input, answers, facts, the rule that decided, and the outcome.

lessons: Removal and referral are separate Nouls because you act on them whatever the intent is.

Only use a secondary answer on the branch it belongs to. The out-of-office reply names another address at 69%, but it is a support inbox, not a referral; names_another_person is read only when the intent is referral.
Get the address with a regex, not the model. Jev decides whether a referral exists; code copies it.
limits: Keep the removal cutoff low. Wrongly suppressing someone costs a reply; emailing an opt-out costs sender reputation and possibly a legal complaint.
Test on your own inbox, including replies in other languages. Jev is strongest in English.
Objections go to a person. Drafting a reply to one needs the raw reply text, which step 3 is not allowed to see.
